messages:
morgan: Anyone else seeing a bunch of dropped model-runtime connections in westus3 (az-b)? Pods reconnecting every ~25-40s, customers reporting inference errors.
jaz: Yep, saw it on the dash. conntrack usage spiked hard around 06:10 UTC.
raj: Alert fired: nf_conntrack > 95% on westus3-nodes.
oncall-bot: Paging eng-infra oncall: incident 2026-03-18-westus3-conntrack
li: Ran `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` on a node, output:
```
259832
nf_conntrack_max: 262144
```
li: `conntrack -L | wc -l` =~ 258k, a lot of TIME_WAIT and some ESTABLISHED entries from 10.32.x.x -> 172.31.x.x: many source ports in 49k-60k range.
morgan: The stack: model-serving pods -> envoy sidecar -> prefetcher sidecar -> outbound cluster egress (SNAT). Hypothesis: prefetcher churn + short-lived outbound connections + limited SNAT ports -> port exhaustion.
jaz: Also seeing many CLOSE_WAIT/CLOSE states on envoy metrics. Looks like half-open from client side; connections not being reused.
raj: Short term mitigation plan:
- scale prefetcher replicas down in westus3 (to reduce churn)
- bump nf_conntrack_max temporarily
- roll pods in az-b to clear stale conntrack entries
li: Executed commands on two nodes:
```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="20000 65535"
```
opsbot: Applied cluster role patch to reduce prefetcher replica count in westus3 to 2
morgan: After scaling down and sysctl bump, conntrack_count dropped to ~120k within 5m and errors decreased.
jaz: Quick note: bumping nf_conntrack_max is a patch, but we need a more durable fix. Root cause still appears to be excessive ephemeral port churn from the sidecar prefetcher using new connections per request.
li: Sample conntrack line showing churn:
```
ipv4     2 tcp      6 431998 TIME_WAIT src=10.32.5.12 dst=172.31.8.9 sport=50132 dport=443 packets=12 bytes=2048 src=172.31.8.9 dst=10.32.5.12 sport=443 dport=50132 packets=10 bytes=1800 mark=0
```
raj: Longer-term mitigations discussed:
- change prefetcher to use connection pooling / keepalive reuse
- move egress to node-local SNAT (one SNAT IP per node) to spread ephemeral ports
- evaluate switching kube-proxy to IPVS where we get fewer NAT hops
- add an alert for nf_conntrack > 70% so we act earlier
morgan: Also consider disabling hairpin SNAT for in-cluster pod->pod egress where not needed; and add per-pod connection limits in sidecar.
jaz: For RDMA nodes: verify whether any hardware offload or proxy is interfering with TCP connection reuse; li can follow up with hw team.
li: Filed a ticket with infra/hw to check RDMA NIC settings and whether offloads cause unexpected conntrack timeouts.
opsbot: Created follow-up playbook: "westus3-conntrack-ephemeral-mitigation" with steps we ran.
morgan: TL;DR: temporary sysctl + scale down prefetcher cleared the immediate pain. Next: connection pooling + node-local egress + alert tuning.
raj: Will schedule a follow-up in eng-infra weekly to track progress. Thanks all :thumbsup:
